topic: Venus day is longer than its year
claim: Venus spins once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225, so its day is longer than its year.

beats.caption: A day on Venus outlasts its year
beats.vo: A day on Venus outlasts its year.

beats.caption: One spin: 243 Earth days. One orbit: 225.
beats.vo: Venus spins so slowly that one full turn takes about 243 Earth days. But one trip around the Sun takes only about 225.

beats.caption: It also spins backward.
beats.vo: It also spins backward compared to Earth. Stand on Venus, and the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.

beats.caption: Surface: about 872°F (467°C)
beats.vo: And you would not enjoy the wait. Its thick atmosphere traps heat, so the surface sits near 872 degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt lead.

beats.caption: Sunrise to sunset: about 117 Earth days
beats.vo: Even sunrise to sunset takes about 117 Earth days. So one Venus day really is longer than a Venus year. Would you wait around for sunset?

sources.text: NASA Science, Venus Facts: https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/ (243-day rotation, 225-day year, 117 days sunrise to sunset, backward spin)
